**In a study, the state of type 2 diabetes of the participants was first determined through interviews and tests. The participants who fasted overnight were then asked to drink a solution with 75 g glucose and their 2-hour blood glucose level was measured, i.e. the blood glucose level two hours after drinking the glucose solution. The waist circumference of the participants was also measured in another test. The bar charts below show the results of the study.
Account for the difference in 2-hour blood glucose level between diagnosed diabetic patients and healthy persons.
Suggest a possible explanation for the difference in 2-hour blood glucose level between the diagnosed diabetic patients and the undiagnosed diabetic patients.
Some scientists proposed that the waist circumference of patients can be used to assess their risk of having type 2 diabetes. Give evidence from the results to support this idea.
Based on your biological knowledge, s
uggest a possible explanation for the relationship between waist circumference and the risk of developing type 2 diabetes.
Without lifestyle intervention, prediabetes can develop into diabetes in a few years. If you were a dietitian, give
pieces of dietary advice to people with prediabetes.
Due to insulin resistance, the body cells of type 2 diabetic patients would not take up extra glucose from blood as effectively as healthy persons.
Therefore, the blood glucose concentration raised to a higher level after the ingestion of glucose solution
and decreased slower than the healthy persons and remained high for a longer period of time / after two hours.
The 2-hour blood glucose level of the diagnosed group is lower than that of the undiagnosed group.
A possible explanation is that the subjects in the diagnosed group may have adopted a healthier lifestyle (e.g. switching to a low GI diet / being more physically active) after the diagnosis.
This helps lower insulin resistance / improve the insulin sensitivity of body cells, which in turn helps take up more glucose from the blood.

The waist circumference of the participants is positively correlated to the 2-hour blood glucose level. / The waist circumferences of diabetic patients among all age groups in the study are significantly higher than that of healthy persons.
Waist circumference can be used as a measure of (abdominal) obesity and obesity is a risk factor for type 2 diabetes.
Avoid food which elevates blood glucose level in a short time (e.g. sweets). /
Limit the portions of food with a high GI (e.g. white rice). /
Eat more foods that are high in dietary fibres (e.g. vegetables).

In Hong Kong, rodent infestation is getting more public attention. Rodent Infestation Rate (RIR) has been a key indicator measuring the extent of the city’s rat problem. It is the ratio of the number of baits bitten by rodents to the total number of baits collected from a survey location. The table below shows the RIR of four districts from 2017 to 2019.

Human papillomavirus (HPV) infection is a common sexually transmitted infection. Persistent HPV infection can cause cervical cancer. There are over 100 types of HPV. Among them, two types,
account for most cases of cervical cancer.

The scientists measured the levels of antibodies against HPV16 and HPV18 in blood of the girls one month and three months after two groups of girls received the last dose of the vaccine. The graph below shows the results.
